name: vault.triage
description: Triage a raw note dumped into the Obsidian inbox: classify its kind, route it to a vault area, and decide whether cheap logic can file it or a frontier LLM must distill it first.

kind.instructions: What kind of artifact this file is

criteria.transcript: Spoken-word capture: meeting, podcast, video, or interview transcript
criteria.scrape: Captured web or app content: articles, forum threads, social posts, docs pages
criteria.code: Source code, scripts, configs, or dumps with substantial code blocks
criteria.log: Machine or agent output: run logs, diffs, command traces, error dumps
criteria.journal: First-person notes: daily notes, ideas, decisions, meeting notes written by a human or agent on purpose
criteria.reference: Structured reference material: research findings, data tables, specifications, curated docs
criteria.junk: Empty stub, fragment, duplicate, or content-free chrome

destination.instructions: Which vault area this file belongs in once filed

criteria.transcripts: It is a spoken-word capture and belongs with the transcripts
criteria.knowledge: Durable reference or curated content the owner will want to link and cite later
criteria.research: Source material feeding an active investigation or content pipeline
criteria.memory: Session, decision, or state record worth remembering but not curated
criteria.archive: Low value but not obviously noise: keep for provenance, out of the working set
criteria.needs_review: Nothing fits confidently; a human should decide where it goes

needs_reasoning.instructions: Turning this file into usable knowledge requires generative reasoning -- summarizing, extracting decisions, rewriting, or reconciling against other notes -- rather than simply filing it where it belongs

is_noise.instructions: This file has no durable value: empty, a UI or export artifact stub, a near-duplicate fragment, or throwaway scratch

sensitivity.instructions: The highest sensitivity level present in the visible text

criteria.public: Already publishable or generic technical content
criteria.internal: Business, project, or agent operations content not meant for public release
criteria.private: Personal health, family, finance, or privately identifiable information about an individual
criteria.secret: Credentials, tokens, keys, or raw passwords appear in the text

rules.reason: credential material visible -- quarantine the file, never index its contents
noise -- archive without a memory write
distillation needed -- hand to a frontier LLM agent, not the filing script
